### bin/test-speed.js

```javascript
// Open https://www.example-url.com in Chrome.
// Press F12 (or Right-Click -> Inspect) to open Developer Tools.
// Click on the Console tab.
// Copy the code below, paste it into the console, and press Enter.

(function() {
    // Wait 500ms to ensure the 'load' event has fully settled
    setTimeout(() => {
        const navData = performance.getEntriesByType('navigation')[0];
        
        if (!navData) {
            console.warn('⚠️ Performance Navigation Timing API not supported.');
            return;
        }

        // Calculate core metrics
        const metrics = {
            'DNS Lookup': (navData.domainLookupEnd - navData.domainLookupStart).toFixed(2) + ' ms',
            'TCP Connection': (navData.connectEnd - navData.connectStart).toFixed(2) + ' ms',
            'TLS/SSL Handshake': navData.secureConnectionStart > 0 
                ? (navData.connectEnd - navData.secureConnectionStart).toFixed(2) + ' ms' 
                : 'N/A (HTTP)',
            'TTFB (Server Response)': (navData.responseStart - navData.requestStart).toFixed(2) + ' ms',
            'DOM Interactive': (navData.domInteractive - navData.startTime).toFixed(2) + ' ms',
            'DOM Content Loaded': (navData.domContentLoadedEventEnd - navData.startTime).toFixed(2) + ' ms',
            'Fully Loaded (Window Load)': (navData.loadEventEnd - navData.startTime).toFixed(2) + ' ms'
        };

        console.clear();
        console.log('%c🚀 Page Performance Metrics', 'color: #00ff00; font-size: 16px; font-weight: bold;');
        console.log('%cTarget: ' + window.location.href, 'color: #00bfff; font-size: 12px;');
        console.table(metrics);

        // Bonus: Resource Summary
        const resources = performance.getEntriesByType('resource');
        const totalRequests = resources.length + 1; // +1 for the main HTML document
        const totalTransferSize = resources.reduce((acc, curr) => acc + (curr.transferSize || curr.encodedBodySize || 0), 0);
        
        console.log('%c📦 Resource Summary', 'color: #ffa500; font-size: 14px; font-weight: bold;');
        console.log(`Total Network Requests: ${totalRequests}`);
        console.log(`Estimated Transfer Size: ${(totalTransferSize / 1024).toFixed(2)} KB`);
        
        console.log('%c💡 Tip: For accurate "First Visit" metrics, open an Incognito window, paste this script, and press Enter immediately.', 'color: #888; font-style: italic;');

    }, 500);
})();
```

### bin/test-speed.php

```php
<?php
/**
 * CLI Web Page Speed Tester
 * Usage: php test-speed.php "https://www.example.com"
 */

// 1. Validate command line arguments
if ($argc < 2) {
    echo "Usage: php test-speed.php <url>\n";
    echo "Example: php test-speed.php https://www.example.com\n";
    echo "Example: php test-speed.php www.example.com\n";
    exit(1);
}

$url = $argv[1];

// 2. Ensure URL has a scheme (http:// or https://)
if (!preg_match('~^(?:f|ht)tps?://~i', $url)) {
    $url = 'https://' . $url;
}

echo "Testing speed for: $url\n";
echo str_repeat("-", 65) . "\n";

// 3. Initialize cURL
$ch = curl_init();
curl_setopt_array($ch, [
    CURLOPT_URL            => $url,
    CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
    CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION => true,      // Follow redirects
    CURLOPT_ENCODING       => "",        // Handle gzip/deflate compression
    CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER => true,      // Verify SSL certificates
    CURLOPT_NOBODY         => false,     // We MUST download the body to measure "Fully Loaded"
    // Realistic User-Agent to avoid 403 Forbidden from strict firewalls (e.g., Cloudflare)
    CURLOPT_USERAGENT      => 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36',
]);

// 4. Execute the request
curl_exec($ch);

// 5. Handle errors
if (curl_errno($ch)) {
    echo "❌ cURL Error: " . curl_error($ch) . "\n";
    curl_close($ch);
    exit(1);
}

// 6. Get timing metrics
$info = curl_getinfo($ch);
curl_close($ch);

// --- Helper Functions ---

// Convert seconds to milliseconds
function ms(float $seconds): string {
    return number_format($seconds * 1000, 2) . ' ms';
}

// Format bytes into human-readable KB/MB
function formatBytes(int $bytes): string {
    if ($bytes <= 0) return 'Unknown';
    $units = ['B', 'KB', 'MB', 'GB'];
    $i = floor(log($bytes, 1024));
    return number_format($bytes / pow(1024, $i), 2) . ' ' . $units[$i];
}

// Get rating for time-based metrics
function getRating(float $ms, float $fastThreshold, float $moderateThreshold): string {
    if ($ms <= $fastThreshold) return "🟢 Fast";
    if ($ms <= $moderateThreshold) return "🟡 Moderate";
    return "🔴 Slow";
}

// Get rating for file size
function getSizeRating(int $bytes): string {
    $mb = $bytes / (1024 * 1024);
    if ($mb < 1.0) return "🟢 Light (< 1 MB)";
    if ($mb < 3.0) return "🟡 Moderate (1 - 3 MB)";
    return "🔴 Heavy (> 3 MB)";
}

// --- Calculations ---

$dnsTime = $info['namelookup_time'];
$tcpTime = $info['connect_time'] - $dnsTime;
$sslTime = $info['pretransfer_time'] - $info['connect_time'];
if ($sslTime < 0) $sslTime = 0; // Fallback for non-HTTPS

$ttfbMs = $info['starttransfer_time'] * 1000;
$totalMs = $info['total_time'] * 1000;

// Page size: prefer uncompressed content length, fallback to downloaded (compressed) size
$pageSize = (int) $info['download_content_length'];
if ($pageSize <= 0) {
    $pageSize = (int) $info['size_download'];
}
$downloadedSize = (int) $info['size_download'];

// 7. Output the results
echo "⏱️  TIMING METRICS:\n";
echo "  • DNS Resolution : " . ms($dnsTime) . "\n";
echo "  • TCP Connect    : " . ms($tcpTime) . "\n";
echo "  • SSL Handshake  : " . ms($sslTime) . "\n";
echo "  • TTFB           : " . ms($info['starttransfer_time']) . " " . getRating($ttfbMs, 200, 600) . "\n";
echo "  • Fully Loaded   : " . ms($info['total_time']) . " " . getRating($totalMs, 1000, 3000) . "\n";

echo str_repeat("-", 65) . "\n";
echo "📊 ADDITIONAL INFO:\n";
echo "  • HTTP Status    : " . $info['http_code'] . "\n";
echo "  • Redirects      : " . $info['redirect_count'] . "\n";
echo "  • Page Size      : " . formatBytes($pageSize) . " " . getSizeRating($pageSize) . "\n";
echo "  • Downloaded     : " . formatBytes($downloadedSize) . " (Compressed over network)\n";
echo "  • Avg Speed      : " . formatBytes((int)$info['speed_download']) . "/s\n";

echo str_repeat("-", 65) . "\n";

// 8. Overall Verdict (Plain English Summary)
echo "💡 OVERALL VERDICT:\n";
$sizeMb = $pageSize / (1024 * 1024);

if ($ttfbMs <= 200 && $totalMs <= 1000 && $sizeMb < 1.0) {
    echo "  🚀 EXCELLENT! Your page loads very fast and is well-optimized.\n";
    echo "     No immediate action required.\n";
} elseif ($ttfbMs <= 600 && $totalMs <= 3000 && $sizeMb < 3.0) {
    echo "  ⚠️  MODERATE. Your page loads acceptably, but there is room for improvement.\n";
    echo "     Consider: compressing images, enabling OPcache, or reviewing database queries.\n";
} else {
    echo "  🐌 SLOW. Your page takes too long to load or is too heavy.\n";
    echo "     Recommended actions:\n";
    echo "     - Check for slow database queries or missing indexes.\n";
    echo "     - Ensure OPcache is enabled in php.ini.\n";
    echo "     - Reduce page size (optimize images/assets).\n";
}
echo str_repeat("-", 65) . "\n";

### config/database.php

```php
<?php
// Load environment variables
\App\Core\Dotenv::load();

$host = \App\Core\Dotenv::required('DB_HOST');
$dbname = \App\Core\Dotenv::required('DB_NAME');
$username = \App\Core\Dotenv::required('DB_USER');
$password = \App\Core\Dotenv::required('DB_PASS');
$charset = \App\Core\Dotenv::get('DB_CHARSET', 'utf8mb4');

$dsn = "mysql:host=$host;dbname=$dbname;charset=$charset";

$options = [
    PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE => PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION,
    PDO::ATTR_DEFAULT_FETCH_MODE => PDO::FETCH_ASSOC,
    PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => false,
];

// Determine if we're in production
$isProduction = 'production';
if (isset($_ENV['APP_ENV'])) {
    $isProduction = $_ENV['APP_ENV'];
}
$isProduction = ($isProduction === 'production');

try {
    $pdo = new PDO($dsn, $username, $password, $options);
} catch (PDOException $e) {
    error_log('Database connection failed: ' . $e->getMessage());
    
    if (!$isProduction) {
        die('Database connection error: ' . $e->getMessage());
    } else {
        http_response_code(503);
        die('Database connection error. Please try again later.');
    }
}

// ✅ RETURN the PDO instance so index.php can receive it
return $pdo;

Since you are building this from scratch, you have total control. Just ensure these 3 things:
Enable OPcache in Production: Add this to your live server's php.ini:

    opcache.enable=1
    opcache.memory_consumption=256
    opcache.interned_strings_buffer=16
    opcache.max_accelerated_files=10000
    opcache.revalidate_freq=0  ; Set to 0 in production
    opcache.validate_timestamps=0  ; Set to 0 in production

<?php
/**
 * Security Configuration
 * 
 * This file contains security settings that can be adjusted based on environment.
 * For production, ensure all security features are enabled.
 */

// Detect environment
$httpHost = '';
if (isset($_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'])) {
    $httpHost = $_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'];
}
$isLocalhost = in_array($httpHost, [
    'localhost',
    '127.0.0.1',
    'onebuild.test',
    'www.onebuild.test',
    'gudangpc.test',
    'www.gudangpc.test',
    'localhost:8080',
    '127.0.0.1:8080',
]);

$isHTTPS = false;
if (!empty($_SERVER['HTTPS']) && $_SERVER['HTTPS'] !== 'off') {
    $isHTTPS = true;
}
if (!empty($_SERVER['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO']) && $_SERVER['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO'] === 'https') {
    $isHTTPS = true;
}

$environment = 'production';
if ($isLocalhost) {
    $environment = 'development';
}
$config = [
    'cookie_secure' => !$isLocalhost && $isHTTPS,
    'cookie_httponly' => true,
    'cookie_samesite' => 'Lax',
    'session_timeout' => 3600,
    'session_regenerate_interval' => 1800,
    'use_strict_mode' => true,
    'force_https' => !$isLocalhost,
    'hsts_enabled' => !$isLocalhost && $isHTTPS,
    'csp_enabled' => true,
    'csp_report_only' => $isLocalhost,
    'is_localhost' => $isLocalhost,
    'is_https' => $isHTTPS,
    'environment' => $environment
];
return $config;

  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS `vendor_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL;

ALTER TABLE `offers`
  ADD CONSTRAINT `offers_ibfk_3` FOREIGN KEY (`vendor_id`) REFERENCES `vendors` (`id`) ON DELETE SET NULL;

-- ===== 012_fix_offers_constraints.sql =====

-- 1. Drop the foreign key constraints that rely on the index
ALTER TABLE `offers` DROP FOREIGN KEY `offers_ibfk_1`;
ALTER TABLE `offers` DROP FOREIGN KEY `offers_ibfk_2`;

-- 2. Drop the old unique index
ALTER TABLE `offers` DROP INDEX `product_store`;

-- 3. Add the new unique index based on vendor
ALTER TABLE `offers` ADD UNIQUE KEY `product_vendor` (`product_id`, `vendor_id`);

-- 4. Re-add the foreign key constraints
ALTER TABLE `offers` 
  ADD CONSTRAINT `offers_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`product_id`) REFERENCES `products` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE;

  ADD CONSTRAINT `offers_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`store_id`) REFERENCES `stores` (`id`);

-- ===== 014_add_indexes.sql =====

-- Add missing performance indexes.
-- Each block checks information_schema first so the migration is safe to run
-- when an equivalent UNIQUE/FOREIGN KEY index already exists.

-- products(slug): already covered by UNIQUE KEY `slug` on the current schema.
SET @idx_exists = (
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.statistics
    WHERE table_schema = DATABASE()
      AND table_name = 'products'
      AND column_name = 'slug'
      AND seq_in_index = 1
);
SET @sql = IF(@idx_exists = 0, 'ALTER TABLE `products` ADD INDEX `idx_products_slug` (`slug`)', 'SELECT 1');
PREPARE stmt FROM @sql;
EXECUTE stmt;
DEALLOCATE PREPARE stmt;

-- offers(product_id): already covered by the leftmost column of UNIQUE KEY `product_vendor`.
SET @idx_exists = (
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.statistics
    WHERE table_schema = DATABASE()
      AND table_name = 'offers'
      AND column_name = 'product_id'
      AND seq_in_index = 1
);
SET @sql = IF(@idx_exists = 0, 'ALTER TABLE `offers` ADD INDEX `idx_offers_product_id` (`product_id`)', 'SELECT 1');
PREPARE stmt FROM @sql;
EXECUTE stmt;
DEALLOCATE PREPARE stmt;

-- offers(vendor_id): already covered by `offers_ibfk_3`.
SET @idx_exists = (
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.statistics
    WHERE table_schema = DATABASE()
      AND table_name = 'offers'
      AND column_name = 'vendor_id'
      AND seq_in_index = 1
);
SET @sql = IF(@idx_exists = 0, 'ALTER TABLE `offers` ADD INDEX `idx_offers_vendor_id` (`vendor_id`)', 'SELECT 1');
PREPARE stmt FROM @sql;
EXECUTE stmt;
DEALLOCATE PREPARE stmt;

-- seo_meta(meta_type, meta_id): already covered by UNIQUE KEY `meta_link`.
SET @idx_exists = (
    SELECT COUNT(*)
    FROM information_schema.statistics s1
    JOIN information_schema.statistics s2
      ON s1.table_schema = s2.table_schema
     AND s1.table_name = s2.table_name
     AND s1.index_name = s2.index_name
    WHERE s1.table_schema = DATABASE()
      AND s1.table_name = 'seo_meta'
      AND s1.column_name = 'meta_type'
      AND s1.seq_in_index = 1
      AND s2.column_name = 'meta_id'
      AND s2.seq_in_index = 2
);
SET @sql = IF(@idx_exists = 0, 'ALTER TABLE `seo_meta` ADD INDEX `idx_seo_meta_type_id` (`meta_type`, `meta_id`)', 'SELECT 1');
PREPARE stmt FROM @sql;
EXECUTE stmt;
DEALLOCATE PREPARE stmt;

-- categories(slug): already covered by UNIQUE KEY `slug`.
SET @idx_exists = (
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.statistics
    WHERE table_schema = DATABASE()
      AND table_name = 'categories'
      AND column_name = 'slug'
      AND seq_in_index = 1
);
SET @sql = IF(@idx_exists = 0, 'ALTER TABLE `categories` ADD INDEX `idx_categories_slug` (`slug`)', 'SELECT 1');
PREPARE stmt FROM @sql;
EXECUTE stmt;
DEALLOCATE PREPARE stmt;

-- vendors(slug): already covered by UNIQUE KEY `slug`.
SET @idx_exists = (
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.statistics
    WHERE table_schema = DATABASE()
      AND table_name = 'vendors'
      AND column_name = 'slug'

ALTER TABLE `user_social_accounts`
  ADD CONSTRAINT `fk_social_user` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `members` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE;

--
-- Constraints for table `vendors`
--
ALTER TABLE `vendors`
  ADD CONSTRAINT `vendors_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`store_id`) REFERENCES `stores` (`id`);

--
-- Constraints for table `wishlists`
--
ALTER TABLE `wishlists`
  ADD CONSTRAINT `wishlists_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`member_id`) REFERENCES `members` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  ADD CONSTRAINT `wishlists_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`product_id`) REFERENCES `products` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE;
```

### database/initial_database.sql

```sql
CREATE TABLE `rate_limits` (
  `id` int(10) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `bucket` varchar(64) NOT NULL,
  `action` varchar(64) NOT NULL,
  `attempt_count` int(10) UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  `window_start` int(10) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci;

CREATE TABLE `users` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `phone` varchar(20) NOT NULL,
  `username` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  `password` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `role` varchar(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'buyer',
  `avatar` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `created_at` timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT current_timestamp(),
  `updated_at` timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT current_timestamp() ON UPDATE current_timestamp(),
  `is_verified` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `last_login_at` datetime DEFAULT NULL
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_general_ci;

ALTER TABLE `rate_limits`
  ADD PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  ADD UNIQUE KEY `uniq_bucket_action` (`bucket`,`action`),
  ADD KEY `idx_window` (`window_start`);

ALTER TABLE `users`
  ADD PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  ADD UNIQUE KEY `username` (`username`);

ALTER TABLE `rate_limits`
  MODIFY `id` int(10) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT;

ALTER TABLE `users`
  MODIFY `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT, AUTO_INCREMENT=2;
```

### docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md

```markdown
# GudangPC: Product Specification

Owner: the PO. This document is the source of truth for **what** is being built.
`AGENTS.md` says **how** to code. If the two conflict, stop and ask.
The worker must not create any table, route, or feature that is not listed for the current task.

---

## 1. What this product is

GudangPC is an Indonesian price-comparison and affiliate website for PC parts and tech gear (CPU, GPU, motherboard, RAM, SSD, PSU, case, cooler, monitor, peripherals). The UI language is English (decision D8).

A visitor finds a product, sees the **same product's prices across several marketplaces** (Tokopedia, Shopee, Lazada, and any other row in `stores`), and clicks through to buy. Every outbound click goes through `/go/<offer_id>`, and the owner earns affiliate commission.

Catalog content is managed by staff in the dashboard. Prices arrive in two ways:

- staff enter and edit offers by hand in the dashboard;
- a **local Python scraper** (`bin/scraper/scrape.py`) writes a CSV file, which staff upload at `/dashboard/products/import`.

There is **no marketplace API integration yet** and no server-side scraping. The scraper runs on a local machine, not on the web server.

### Success looks like

- A visitor lands on a product page from Google and sees a clear price table with a Buy button per seller.
- Staff can add a product with 3 offers in under 3 minutes from the dashboard.
- The owner can see which products and marketplaces get the most clicks.

### Not what this is

Not a shop: no cart, checkout, payments, stock management, or first-party reviews. No email is sent by the application. There are no public marketplace or seller pages (decision D5).

---

## 2. Vocabulary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Marketplace** | A row in `stores` (Tokopedia, Shopee, Lazada, ...). The word "store" in table and class names means marketplace. |
| **Seller** | A row in `vendors`. Every seller belongs to exactly one marketplace (`vendors.store_id`). |
| **Offer** (listing) | One seller's price for one product on one marketplace. One row in `offers`. |
| **Member** | A public user account, stored in `members`. Not a staff account. |

The physical table and class names (`stores`, `StoreModel`, `vendors`, `VendorModel`) stay as they are. Only the documentation vocabulary changes.

---

## 3. People and roles

| Role | Stored in | Signs in with | Can do |
|---|---|---|---|
| `root` | `users.role = 'root'` | Phone number | Everything. Create and manage admins and members. |
| `admin` | `users.role = 'admin'` | Phone number | Manage the catalog (categories, brands, marketplaces, sellers, products, offers, CSV import). Cannot touch `root` or `admin` accounts. |
| `member` | `members`, session role value `visitor` | Email | Browse the public site, open the Member Area at `/member`, edit own profile, use the wishlist. Cannot open the dashboard. |
| anonymous | none | - | Browse, search, click Buy. No account needed. |

### Registration and activation

- Members register themselves at `/register` with **email**, a password and a **WhatsApp number**. A new row is created with status `pending`.
- A `root` administrator activates the member in Dashboard -> Members (the Members module is restricted to `root` today). Only `active` members can sign in; `banned` members cannot.
- Staff accounts are not self-registered. The first `root` is created with `bin/add_root.php`; `admin` accounts are created from the dashboard by the `root`.
- `/login` accepts either an email address (member) or an E.164 phone number such as `+628123456789` (staff).
- Google sign-ups are auto-activated, email sign-ups stay pending.

Wishlist URLs are public routes, but they only work for a signed-in member (session role `visitor`).

---

## 4. Status vocabulary

| Table | Column | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `categories`, `brands`, `stores`, `products`, `offers` | `status` | `draft`, `published` |
| `vendors` | `status` | `active` (deliberate exception; default `active`) |
| `members` | `status` | `pending`, `active`, `banned` |
| `seo_meta` | `robots_tag` | free text, default `index, follow` |

Public pages show only `published` rows (and only `active` sellers). Members must be `active` to sign in.

Non-members are not stored anywhere; a visitor is anonymous until they register.

---

## 5. Active offer (decision D3)

This is the **single definition** of a trustworthy, publicly visible offer. It lives in one place in `OfferModel` and is used by every page, query and redirect.

An offer is *active* when **all** of the following are true:

1. `offers.status = 'published'`
2. `offers.in_stock = 1`
3. its marketplace (`stores`) has `status = 'published'`
4. its seller is missing, or its seller (`vendors`) has `status = 'active'`
5. `offers.last_checked_at` is NULL, or it is within the last 14 days

Public price tables, price badges, the homepage, the sitemap and structured data use only active offers. An offer whose data is older than 14 days is *stale* and must not be shown publicly.

---

## 6. Decisions (D1, D4 to D10)

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| D1 | **The compare feature is removed**: its route, UI, controller and view. Parked until per-category specs exist. |
| D4 | A product with **no active offer** is shown dimmed on category, brand and search pages, hidden on the homepage, left out of `sitemap.xml`, and has no price in structured data. |
| D5 | **No public pages for marketplaces or sellers** for now. Their SEO fields stay in the dashboard but nothing renders them publicly. |
| D6 | The unique rule `(product_id, vendor_id)` on `offers` stays. A second listing from the same seller for the same product is **reported**, not merged. |
| D7 | Affiliate links are built from a per-marketplace **template** (`stores.affiliate_url_template`) applied to the raw product URL. If no template exists, the raw URL is used and the import report warns. |
| D8 | UI language stays **English**. Indonesian UI is parked. |
| D9 | The canonical URL is **computed at render time** from `APP_URL`. A stored `seo_meta.canonical_url` is honoured only if it is absolute (starts with `http`). |
| D10 | Google sign-ins verify and clear OAuth state, verify TLS with a 10-second timeout, require a verified email, create new members as `active`, and activate a pending email member with a random password. |

D2 is not a change: the wishlist stays, and members still register as `pending` until a `root` administrator activates them.

---

## 7. Global rules for all modules

- **Money:** Rupiah stored as an unsigned integer in `price_idr`. No decimals, no floats. Display with `number_format($price, 0, ',', '.')` and the prefix `Rp `.
- **Slugs:** lowercase `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`; unique per table; created from the name; not changed automatically on rename.
- **Charset:** `utf8mb4`, collation `utf8mb4_unicode_ci`, engine InnoDB, except the legacy `users` table which is `utf8mb4_general_ci` in `initial_database.sql`.
- **Timestamps:** every table has `created_at` and `updated_at`, except `offer_clicks` (only `clicked_at`), `wishlists` and `search_cache` (only `created_at`), and the planned `price_history` (only `recorded_at`).
- **Affiliate links:** public pages never print an affiliate URL directly. They link to `/go/<offer_id>`. Outbound links use `target="_blank"` and `rel="sponsored nofollow noopener"`. Pages with offers show the disclosure line: "We may earn a commission from purchases made through our links."
- **Offer visibility:** only active offers (section 5) are shown publicly.
- **Output safety:** all dynamic output is escaped. Rich descriptions are printed only after `\App\Core\RichText::clean()`.
- **Deleting content:** a category cannot be deleted while products reference it. A marketplace cannot be deleted while offers or sellers reference it. A brand is not blocked; products pointing at it get `brand_id = NULL`. Products and offers are hard-deleted from the dashboard after a confirm. An offer that already has click history must not be deleted; set it to Draft or Out of stock instead (task A4).
- **Pagination:** public lists paginate at 20 per page with `?page=N` (planned in C4). The admin product list paginates at 20 per page (planned in E2).

---

## 8. Data model (as built today)

Existing tables and columns, as created by `database/initial_database.sql` and migrations `002` to `018`.

### `users` (staff: root and admin)

```
id, phone, username, password, role, avatar, is_verified, last_login_at,
created_at, updated_at
PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE (username)
```

`role` holds `root` or `admin`. The column default is `buyer` in the SQL file; the application only creates `root` and `admin`.

### `rate_limits`

```
id, bucket, action, attempt_count, window_start, created_at, updated_at
PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE (bucket, action), KEY (window_start)
```

### `categories`

```
id, parent_id, name, slug, description, image, image_alt, sort_order,
status, created_at, updated_at
PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE (slug)
```

`parent_id` exists but is not used by the public site yet.

### `brands`

```
id, name, slug, logo, website_url, description, status,
created_by, updated_by, created_at, updated_at
PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE (slug)
```

### `stores` (marketplaces)

```
id, name, slug, description, logo, base_url, status,
created_by, updated_by, created_at, updated_at
PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE (slug)
```

### `vendors` (sellers)

```
id, store_id, name, slug, rating, store_rating, status,
created_at, updated_at
PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE (slug), KEY (store_id)
FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES stores (id)
```

`status` default is `active`. `rating` and `store_rating` are decimal ratings carried from marketplace data; the importer updates `store_rating` from the scrape.

### `products`

```
id, category_id, brand_id, name, slug, model_number, short_description,
description, image, image_alt, search_tags, status,
created_by, updated_by, created_at, updated_at
PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE (slug), KEY (category_id), KEY (brand_id)
FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES categories (id)
FOREIGN KEY (brand_id) REFERENCES brands (id) ON DELETE SET NULL
```

### `offers`

```
id, product_id, store_id, vendor_id, price_idr, affiliate_url,
seller_title, seller_name, seller_rating, product_rating, sold_count,
in_stock, last_checked_at, status, created_at, updated_at
PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE (product_id, vendor_id), KEY (store_id)
FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES products (id) ON DELETE CASCADE
FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES stores (id)
FOREIGN KEY (vendor_id) REFERENCES vendors (id) ON DELETE SET NULL
```

`seller_name` and `seller_rating` are legacy per-offer seller fields kept alongside `vendor_id`. `seller_title`, `product_rating` and `sold_count` are scraped listing data. `offer_clicks` cascades from `offers`.

### `offer_clicks`

```
id, offer_id, clicked_at, ip_hash, user_agent, referer
PRIMARY KEY (id), KEY (offer_id)
FOREIGN KEY (offer_id) REFERENCES offers (id) ON DELETE CASCADE
```

`ip_hash` = `hash('sha256', $ip . <APP_SALT from .env>)`. Raw IPs are never stored. No `updated_at`.

### `seo_meta`

```
id, meta_type, meta_id, seo_title, seo_description, canonical_url, robots_tag,
og_title, og_description, og_image, twitter_title, twitter_description,
schema_markup, custom_head_tags, custom_body, custom_footer,
created_at, updated_at
PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE (meta_type, meta_id)
```

`meta_type` is the module name (`product`, `category`, `brand`, `store`). `custom_body` and `custom_footer` are admin-authored HTML.

### `settings`

```
id, setting_key, setting_value, created_at, updated_at
PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE (setting_key)
```

### `members`

```
id, email, username, password, status, verification_token, avatar, whatsapp,
created_at, updated_at
PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE (email), UNIQUE (username)
```

`status` default is `pending`. `whatsapp` is collected at registration.

### `wishlists`

```
id, member_id, product_id, created_at
PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE (member_id, product_id), KEY (member_id), KEY (product_id)
FOREIGN KEY (member_id) REFERENCES members (id) ON DELETE CASCADE
FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES products (id) ON DELETE CASCADE

No `updated_at`.

### `search_cache` (currently unused)

```
id, query_hash, original_query, parsed_intent, created_at
PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE (query_hash)
```

`SearchCacheModel` exists but nothing reads or writes it. `products.search_tags` is a plain text column used by search.

### Planned schema (not yet applied)

**Migration 021** adds listing identity and affiliate templates:

- `offers.source_url` `text` NULL: the scraped product page URL;
- `offers.external_id` `varchar(100)` NULL: the marketplace listing id;
- unique key `(store_id, external_id)` on `offers` (NULL `external_id` rows may repeat);
- `stores.affiliate_url_template` `varchar(500)` NULL.

**Migration 022** adds price history:

- `price_history`: `id`, `offer_id` (`ON DELETE CASCADE`), `price_idr bigint unsigned`, `recorded_at datetime`;
- index on `(offer_id, recorded_at)`; no `created_at` / `updated_at`.

### Not in the database

`spec_definitions`, `product_specs` and any `home` table do not exist. Specs and compare are parked.

---

## 9. URL map

### Public (no login)

| URL | Serves |
|---|---|
| `/` | Homepage |
| `/categories` | Category list |
| `/brands` | Brand list |
| `/brand/<slug>` | Brand page |
| `/<category-slug>` | Category page |
| `/<category-slug>/<product-slug>` | Product detail page |
| `/search?q=` | Search results |
| `/go/<offer_id>` | Logs the click, then 302 redirects to the offer's affiliate URL |
| `/register` | Member registration form (GET) and `/register/submit` (POST) |
| `/login` | Sign-in form (GET) and `/login/submit` (POST); `/logout` (POST) |
| `/member` | Member Area |
| `/member/profile` | Own member profile |
| `/wishlist/add/<id>` | Add a product to the wishlist (member only) |
| `/wishlist/remove/<id>` | Remove a product from the wishlist (member only) |
| `/sitemap.xml` | XML sitemap (planned, task A6) |

### Dashboard (login required; admin or root)

| URL | Module |
|---|---|
| `/dashboard` | Overview |
| `/dashboard/profile` | Own staff profile |
| `/dashboard/admins[...]` | Staff accounts (root only) |
| `/dashboard/members` | Members; `/activate` and `/ban` actions (root only) |
| `/dashboard/categories[...]` | Categories |
| `/dashboard/brands[...]` | Brands |
| `/dashboard/stores[...]` | Marketplaces |
| `/dashboard/vendors[...]` | Sellers |
| `/dashboard/products[...]` | Products, plus offer add/delete inside the product edit page (offer edit planned, task A4) |
| `/dashboard/products/import` | CSV import form; `/store` handles the upload |
| `/dashboard/settings` | Settings |
| `/dashboard/clicks` | Click analytics (planned, task E1) |

`[...]` means the standard CRUD pattern from `AGENTS.md`: list, `create`, `store`, `(<id>)/edit`, `(<id>)/update`, `(<id>)/delete`.

---

## 10. Roadmap

The PO splits each phase into small tasks. The worker only ever sees the current task.

| Phase | Tasks | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | T0.1 | Make this spec match reality |
| A | A1 to A6 | Bugs and security: member registration, description output, one active-offer definition with freshness, offer editing with protected click history, hardened `/go/`, `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml` |
| B | B1 to B4 | SEO output: helper and layout tags, wiring into pages, canonical clean-up and product URL redirect, breadcrumbs and structured data |
| C | C1 to C7 | Browse experience: navbar clean-up, remove compare, product cards with prices, pagination and sorting, better search, homepage sections, product page polish |
| D | D1 to D5 | Import engine: migrations for listing identity and affiliate templates, marketplace template field, importer hardening, price history, scraper update |
| E | E1 and E2 | Dashboard: overview counters and click analytics, product list filters and pagination |

### Parked (do not build until the PO writes a task)

1. **Import review queue:** unmatched scraped rows go to a staging table; staff match each row to a product with a search box; the listing (`store_id` + `external_id`) is remembered so the next scrape matches automatically.
2. **Image mirroring:** download and convert the scraper's `image_url` (signed marketplace URLs expire); decide whether seller images are acceptable.
3. **Specs and compare:** `spec_definitions` per category, specs on products, then compare within one category only.
4. **Price chart and price-drop alerts** for members (needs price history and a way to reach members).
5. **Indonesian UI** and Indonesian meta titles (`<html lang="id">`).
6. **Public marketplace and seller pages.**
7. **Member onboarding:** decide between admin activation (today), automatic activation, or WhatsApp verification.
8. **A migration runner** (`bin/migrate.php` plus a `migrations` table); today migrations are run by hand and migration 012 depends on constraint names.
9. **Caching** of the homepage queries.

---

## 11. Phase gate

A phase is **done** only when every task report is accepted by the PO, `php bin/check_rules.php` passes on the whole project, and the PO has clicked through every manual test step.
```

### docs/semantic-html-tags.md

```markdown
# Complete List of Semantic HTML Tags

Semantic HTML tags define the meaning and structure of web content rather than just its visual appearance. Using these tags helps search engines, AI crawlers, and screen readers accurately parse and understand your pages.

---

## 1. Page Layout & Sectioning
* **`<header>`**: Defines introductory content or a group of navigation links for a page or section.
* **`<nav>`**: Marks a block of major navigation links, such as a main menu or table of contents.
* **`<main>`**: Wraps the dominant, unique content of the page (use only one per page).
* **`<article>`**: Identifies self-contained content that makes sense on its own (e.g., a blog post, forum comment, or product card).
* **`<section>`**: Groups related content thematically, typically paired with a heading.
* **`<aside>`**: Marks content indirectly related to the main text, such as sidebars, callout boxes, or ad blocks.
* **`<footer>`**: Defines the closing area for a page or section, usually holding copyright info, author details, or secondary links.
* **`<search>`**: Wraps a section containing search form controls and filtering tools.
* **`<address>`**: Provides contact information for the nearest `<article>` or the entire `<body>`.

## 2. Headings & Text Grouping
* **`<h1>` to `<h6>`**: Establishes a strict six-level outline hierarchy for page titles and subheadings.
* **`<hgroup>`**: Groups a primary heading with secondary subheadings or taglines.
* **`<p>`**: Defines a standard paragraph of text.
* **`<blockquote>`**: Marks a long quotation from an external source, often paired with a `cite` attribute.
* **`<pre>`**: Preserves exact whitespace and line breaks, commonly used for code blocks.
* **`<hr>`**: Represents a thematic break or topic shift between paragraphs.

## 3. Lists & Data Tables
* **`<ul>`**: Creates an unordered bulleted list where item sequence does not matter.
* **`<ol>`**: Creates an ordered numbered list for step-by-step instructions or rankings.
* **`<li>`**: Defines an individual item inside a `<ul>`, `<ol>`, or `<menu>`.
* **`<menu>`**: Marks an unordered list of interactive commands or toolbar buttons.
* **`<dl>`**: Wraps a description list of terms and their definitions.
* **`<dt>`**: Identifies the term or name being defined inside a `<dl>`.
* **`<dd>`**: Provides the description or value for the preceding `<dt>`.
* **`<table>`**: Defines tabular data organized into rows and columns.
* **`<caption>`**: Adds an accessible title or summary to a `<table>`.
* **`<thead>`**: Groups header rows within a table.
* **`<tbody>`**: Groups main body data rows within a table.
* **`<tfoot>`**: Groups summary or footer rows within a table.
* **`<tr>`**: Defines a row of cells in a table.
* **`<th>`**: Defines a header cell in a table.
* **`<td>`**: Defines a standard data cell in a table.
* **`<colgroup>`**: Groups one or more columns in a table for formatting.
* **`<col>`**: Defines column properties for each column within a `<colgroup>`.

## 4. Inline Text Semantics
* **`<a>`**: Creates a hyperlink to another page, file, or anchor point.
* **`<strong>`**: Indicates text with strong importance, seriousness, or urgency.
* **`<em>`**: Adds stress emphasis that changes the spoken meaning of a sentence.
* **`<mark>`**: Highlights text for reference or relevance within a specific context.
* **`<cite>`**: Marks the title of a creative work (e.g., a book, song, movie, or research paper).
* **`<q>`**: Wraps a short inline quotation.
* **`<abbr>`**: Identifies an abbreviation or acronym, optionally providing the full expansion via the `title` attribute.
* **`<dfn>`**: Marks the specific instance where a term is being defined in a sentence.
* **`<time>`**: Represents a specific date, time, or duration in a machine-readable format (`datetime`).
* **`<data>`**: Links visible content with a machine-readable translation via the `value` attribute.
* **`<code>`**: Marks a short fragment of computer code.
* **`<var>`**: Represents the name of a variable in a mathematical expression or programming context.
* **`<samp>`**: Represents sample or quoted output from a computer program.
* **`<kbd>`**: Represents user input from a keyboard, voice input, or other text entry device.
* **`<sub>`**: Defines subscript text (e.g., chemical formulas like `H2O`).
* **`<sup>`**: Defines superscript text (e.g., exponents or footnotes).
* **`<small>`**: Represents side comments, disclaimers, and fine print.
* **`<s>`**: Marks content that is no longer accurate or relevant (e.g., a strikethrough price).
* **`<del>`**: Tracks text that has been deleted from a document.
* **`<ins>`**: Tracks text that has been added to a document.
* **`<ruby>`**: Represents small annotations rendered above, below, or next to base text (often used for East Asian typography).
* **`<rt>`**: Specifies the ruby text component of a `<ruby>` annotation.
* **`<rp>`**: Provides fallback parentheses for browsers that do not support `<ruby>` annotations.
* **`<bdi>`**: Isolates a span of text that might be formatted in a different text direction from surrounding text.
* **`<bdo>`**: Overrides the current text directionality (left-to-right or right-to-left).
* **`<wbr>`**: Suggests an optional line-break opportunity inside long words or URLs.

## 5. Media & Embedded Content
* **`<figure>`**: Wraps self-contained media (images, diagrams, code snippets) referenced as a single unit.
* **`<figcaption>`**: Provides a caption or legend describing the contents of its parent `<figure>`.
* **`<img>`**: Embeds an image, using the `alt` attribute to provide a text description for bots and screen readers.
* **`<picture>`**: Contains zero or more `<source>` elements and one `<img>` element to offer responsive image versions.
* **`<source>`**: Specifies multiple media resources for `<picture>`, `<audio>`, or `<video>` elements.
* **`<video>`**: Embeds a native media player for video playback.
* **`<audio>`**: Embeds a native sound player for audio content.
* **`<track>`**: Attaches timed text tracks (subtitles, captions, chapters) to `<video>` and `<audio>`.
* **`<iframe>`**: Embeds another HTML page inside the current document.
* **`<svg>`**: Defines a container for Scalable Vector Graphics.
* **`<math>`**: Top-level element for rendering MathML mathematical formulas.
* **`<map>`**: Defines an image map with clickable link areas.
* **`<area>`**: Defines a clickable hotspot region inside an image `<map>`.

## 6. Interactive & Disclosure Elements
* **`<details>`**: Creates a native disclosure widget in which information is visible only when toggled open.
* **`<summary>`**: Specifies a visible heading or toggle label for a `<details>` element.
* **`<dialog>`**: Represents a modal or non-modal dialog box or popup window.

## 7. Forms & User Input
* **`<form>`**: Wraps interactive controls for submitting user information.
* **`<label>`**: Binds a descriptive text caption directly to a form control.
* **`<fieldset>`**: Groups several related controls and labels within a web form.
* **`<legend>`**: Represents a caption for the content of its parent `<fieldset>`.
* **`<input>`**: Creates interactive controls for web-based forms to accept data from the user.
* **`<textarea>`**: Represents a multi-line plain-text editing control.
* **`<select>`**: Represents a control that provides a menu of options.
* **`<option>`**: Defines an item contained in a `<select>`, `<optgroup>`, or `<datalist>`.
* **`<optgroup>`**: Creates a grouping of options within a `<select>` element.
* **`<button>`**: Creates an interactive button for submitting forms or triggering actions.
* **`<datalist>`**: Contains a set of `<option>` elements that represent permissible or recommended choices for other controls.
* **`<output>`**: Container element into which a site or app can inject the results of a calculation or user action.
* **`<progress>`**: Displays an indicator showing the completion progress of a task.
* **`<meter>`**: Represents either a scalar value within a known range or a fractional value.

---

## Reference: Non-Semantic Tags (Avoid for Structure)
* **`<div>`**: Generic block-level container with no semantic meaning (use only for layout/CSS styling hooks).
* **`<span>`**: Generic inline container with no semantic meaning (use only for styling hooks).
* **`<b>`, `<i>`, `<u>`**: Legacy formatting tags that change visual style without signaling importance or emphasis.
```

## 1. Decisions baked into this pack (veto before you start)

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| D1 | **Compare feature is removed** (routes, UI, controller, view). Parked until per-category specs exist. |

| D3 | **Active offer** = offer `published` AND `in_stock = 1` AND marketplace (`stores`) `published` AND seller (`vendors`) `active` (or no vendor) AND `last_checked_at` within 14 days (or NULL). One definition, in `OfferModel`, used everywhere. |
| D4 | Products with **no active offer**: shown dimmed on category/brand/search pages, hidden on the homepage, left out of `sitemap.xml`, no price in structured data. |
| D5 | **No public pages for stores/vendors** for now. Their SEO fields stay in the dashboard but nothing renders them. |
| D6 | Unique rule `(product_id, vendor_id)` stays. A second listing from the same seller for the same product is **reported**, not merged. |
| D7 | Affiliate links: a per-marketplace **template** builds the link from the raw product URL. If no template exists, the raw URL is used and the import report warns. |
| D8 | UI language stays **English** for now (parked: Indonesian UI). |
| D9 | Canonical URL is **computed at render time** from `APP_URL`; stored canonical values are only honoured if they are absolute (`http...`). |

Vocabulary used in this pack: **Marketplace** = a row in `stores` (Tokopedia, Shopee, Lazada). **Seller** = a row in `vendors` (belongs to one marketplace). Table and class names do not change.

# PHASE A: Bugs, security, offer rules

## A1: Fix member registration (always fails today)

**Bug:** in `app/Controllers/AuthController.php`, method `register()`, the code does `Validator::sanitize($whatsapp, 20)` on the empty variable instead of the posted value, so the WhatsApp check always fails and **nobody can register**.

**Read first:** `AuthController.php` (`register`), `views/auth/register.php`, `app/Core/RateLimiter.php` (signature of `consume`).

**Change (only `AuthController.php`):**
1. Read `$_POST['whatsapp']` into a raw variable (default `''`), sanitize it (max 30), then remove spaces and dashes with `preg_replace('/[\s\-]/', '', ...)` before the existing regex check.
2. Keep the existing regex rule and error message.
3. The registration rate limit currently uses one global bucket (`consume('register', 'register')`): one attacker blocks everyone. Use the visitor's `REMOTE_ADDR` (string, default `''`) as the identifier instead of the literal `'register'`; keep the action name `'register'`.

**Do not:** touch login, email verification, or the member model.

**Manual test:**
1. Register with `+628123456789`, valid email, 8+ char password → redirected to login with the "administrator must activate" message.
2. Check the `members` row: status `pending`, `whatsapp` filled.
3. Register again with `0812 3456 789` (spaces) and another email → accepted, stored without spaces.
4. Register with `abc` as WhatsApp → error shown.
5. Dashboard → Members → activate the member → member can log in.

## A2: Stop raw description output (stored XSS risk)

**Problem:** `views/public/products/show.php` prints `$descriptionValue` unescaped. The admin form cleans it, but `ProductImporter` writes CSV `description` straight into the database. Category and brand pages already use `\App\Core\RichText::clean()`.

**Files:** `views/public/products/show.php`, `app/Core/ProductImporter.php` (protected, this task authorizes it).

**Change:**
1. In the view, compute `$descriptionHtml = \App\Core\RichText::clean($descriptionValue);` in the PHP block at the top and print that instead. Add the same one-line comment style used in `views/public/categories/show.php` ("cleaned by RichText::clean(); only unescaped output on this page"). Keep the empty-description fallback text.
2. In `ProductImporter.php`, there are **two** places that do `$productData['description'] = $description;`. In both, wrap the value in `RichText::clean(...)` (same namespace, no `use` needed). Do not refactor the duplicated block.

**Manual test:**
1. In phpMyAdmin set a product description to `<p>Hi</p><script>alert(1)</script><a href="javascript:alert(2)">x</a>`.
2. Open the product page: no alert, no script tag in page source, the link has no `href`.
3. Product with a normal description still renders paragraphs.

## A3: One definition of "active offer" + freshness

**Goal:** public pages must only show offers that are trustworthy (decision D3). Today the public query ignores `offers.status`, marketplace status, seller status and age; admin-created offers are `draft` while imported ones are `published`; importer skips `last_checked_at` for unchanged rows.

**Files created:** `database/migrations/019_offer_status_and_freshness.sql`
**Files changed:** `app/Models/OfferModel.php`, `app/Controllers/AdminProductController.php`, `views/dashboard/products/edit.php`, `app/Core/ProductImporter.php` (protected, authorized).

**Migration 019 (idempotent):**
```sql
UPDATE offers SET status = 'published' WHERE status = 'draft';
UPDATE offers SET last_checked_at = updated_at WHERE last_checked_at IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE offers MODIFY COLUMN status varchar(20) DEFAULT 'published';
```

**`OfferModel`:**
1. Add `public static function activeCondition(): string` returning exactly this SQL fragment (aliases `o`, `s`, `v` are used by every caller):
```
o.status = 'published' AND o.in_stock = 1 AND s.status = 'published' AND (v.id IS NULL OR v.status = 'active') AND (o.last_checked_at IS NULL OR o.last_checked_at >= DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 14 DAY))
```
2. Change `findPublicByProductId()` to use it (keep the joins and `ORDER BY o.price_idr ASC`). Also select `v.store_rating AS vendor_store_rating` in that query.
3. Add `public function findActiveById(int $offerId): ?array`: same joins, `WHERE o.id = ? AND ` + active condition, returns the offer row or `null`.
4. Add `public function countActive(): int` and `public function countStale(): int` (published offers, `in_stock = 1`, with `last_checked_at < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 14 DAY)`). These are used later by the dashboard.

**`AdminProductController::storeOffer`:** when inserting an offer also set `'status' => 'published'` and `'last_checked_at' => date('Y-m-d H:i:s')`.

**`views/dashboard/products/edit.php`:** in the offers table add two columns: **Status** and **Last checked** (show the datetime or `-`). Nothing else.

**`ProductImporter.php`:** in the branch that counts `skippedIdenticalOffers`, the offer is not touched, so `last_checked_at` stays old and the offer would expire after 14 days even though the scraper just confirmed it. Add a private method `touchOffer(int $offerId): void` (`UPDATE offers SET last_checked_at = ?, in_stock = 1 WHERE id = ?`) and call it in that branch when not in dry-run. Also set `in_stock = 1` in `updateOffer()` (an offer seen again is in stock).

**PO step after the task:** run migration 019.

**Manual test:**
1. Product with 2 offers → both still visible publicly after migration.
2. Set one offer's `last_checked_at` to 30 days ago in phpMyAdmin → it disappears from the public price table.
3. Set a marketplace to `draft` → its offers disappear; set back to `published`.
4. Import the same CSV twice → second run reports identical rows; `last_checked_at` of those offers updated to now.
5. Add an offer in the dashboard → shows `published` and a last-checked time.

## A4: Edit offers in the dashboard + protect click history

**Problem:** there is no way to edit an offer (only add or delete). Deleting and re-adding is the only way to change a price, and `offer_clicks` has `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so every correction **wipes that offer's click history**.

**Files changed:** `public/index.php` (routes), `app/Controllers/AdminProductController.php`, `app/Models/ClickModel.php`, `views/dashboard/products/edit.php`.

**Route (add inside the Products block, after the existing offer routes):**
`$router->addRoute('dashboard/products/(\d+)/offer/(\d+)/update', 'AdminProductController', 'updateOffer');`

**`AdminProductController::updateOffer(string $productId, string $offerId): void`** (follow the pattern of `storeOffer`: requireAdmin, POST check, CSRF):
- Load the offer; it must belong to the product, otherwise error + redirect.
- Editable fields: `price_idr` (`Validator::integer(..., 1)`), `affiliate_url` (`Validator::sanitize` 5000 + `Validator::url`), `in_stock` (checkbox), `status` (`Validator::inArray` of `draft`, `published`). Store and seller are **not** editable.
- Set `last_checked_at` to now. Flash success/error, redirect to the product edit page.

**`ClickModel`:** add `public function countByOfferId(int $offerId): int`.

**`AdminProductController::deleteOffer`:** if `countByOfferId() > 0`, do not delete; set `$_SESSION['error'] = 'This offer has click history. Set it to Draft or Out of stock instead.'` and redirect.

**View:** each offer row gets an **Edit** button that opens a Bootstrap modal (`data-bs-toggle="modal"`, no inline JS) with a form (CSRF hidden input) posting to the new route. Use a unique modal id per offer (`offer-edit-<id>`). Keep the existing delete confirm modal.

**Manual test:**
1. Edit an offer's price → saved; public page shows the new price.
2. Tick "out of stock" → offer disappears publicly.
3. Click the offer's Buy button on the public page (creates a click), then try to delete the offer in the dashboard → refused with the message.
4. Delete an offer with zero clicks → works.
5. Try to edit an offer id that belongs to another product (change the URL by hand) → "Offer not found".

## A5: Harden `/go/<offer_id>`

**Problem:** `PublicProductController::go()` redirects to any offer of a published product, even out-of-stock/draft/expired ones, logs crawler hits as clicks, and is not excluded from robots.

**Files changed:** `app/Controllers/PublicProductController.php`.

**Change `go()`:**
1. Use `OfferModel::findActiveById()`. If it returns `null`:
   - if the offer exists and its product is published → flash `$_SESSION['error'] = 'That offer is no longer available.'` and redirect to the product page (`/<category_slug>/<product_slug>`, load with `ProductModel::findByIdWithRelations`);
   - otherwise render the existing 404.
2. Add `private function isBot(string $userAgent): bool` (case-insensitive substring match against: `bot`, `crawl`, `spider`, `slurp`, `preview`, `facebookexternalhit`, `curl`, `wget`, `python-requests`, `headless`; an empty user agent counts as a bot). If it is a bot: **do not log**, still redirect.
3. Before redirecting send `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` and `Cache-Control: no-store`.
4. Keep the 302 redirect and the existing hashing of the IP.

**Manual test:**
1. Click Buy on an active offer → redirect works, one new row in `offer_clicks`.
2. `curl -I <site>/go/<id>` (curl user agent) → redirect header present, **no** new click row, `X-Robots-Tag` present.
3. Mark the offer out of stock, open `/go/<id>` → back on the product page with the error message.
4. `/go/999999` → 404.

## A6: Fix `robots.txt` and add `sitemap.xml`

**Problems:** `public/robots.txt` disallows `/admin/` (the dashboard is `/dashboard`), points `Sitemap:` at another project's domain, references a `security.txt` that does not exist, and does not block `/go/`. There is no sitemap.

**Files changed:** `public/robots.txt`, `public/index.php`.

**`robots.txt`:** keep the per-bot structure, but in every section replace the disallow list with: `/dashboard`, `/login`, `/logout`, `/register`, `/member`, `/go/`, `/search`, `/wishlist/`. Replace the `Sitemap:` line with `Sitemap: https://REPLACE-ME/sitemap.xml` (the PO edits the domain by hand; the worker must not invent a domain). Remove the `Security:` line.

**Route** (before the wildcard routes): `$router->addRoute('sitemap\.xml', 'SitemapController', 'index');`

**`SitemapController::index()`:** send `Content-Type: application/xml; charset=UTF-8`. Base = `\App\Core\Dotenv::get('APP_URL', '')`; if empty, output a 500-style plain message "APP_URL is not set" with `http_response_code(500)`. URLs (all absolute, XML-escaped, with `<lastmod>` from `updated_at` where available):

- each published category `/<slug>`
- each published brand `/brand/<slug>`

3. `/robots.txt` shows the new paths and the placeholder sitemap line; replace the domain by hand.

# PHASE B: SEO output

Background: SEO fields are saved by the four admin controllers (`product`, `category`, `brand`, `store` in table `seo_meta`) but **nothing prints them**. Only the product page reads `seo_title` and `seo_description`. `views/layouts/header.php` prints only `<title>` and `description`. Category and brand controllers never load SEO. There is no public store page (decision D5).

## B1: SEO helper and layout output

**Files created:** `app/Core/Seo.php` (protected folder, authorized).
**Files changed:** `views/layouts/header.php`, `views/layouts/footer.php`.

**`App\Core\Seo` (all `public static`, with docblocks):**
- `absoluteUrl(string $path): string`: `APP_URL` (from `Dotenv::get('APP_URL', '')`, trailing slash trimmed) + path (ensure one leading slash). Return `''` if `APP_URL` is empty.
- `plainText(string $html, int $max): string`: `strip_tags`, decode entities, collapse whitespace, trim, cut to `$max` characters on a word boundary with `mb_*` functions.
- `cleanJsonLd(string $raw): string`: trim; return `''` if empty; `json_decode` it; if invalid return `''`; otherwise return `json_encode($decoded, JSON_HEX_TAG | JSON_HEX_AMP | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE)`.

**`header.php` new optional variables** (default each with the existing `isset()` pattern): `$seo` (array or null), `$canonicalUrl` (string), `$ogImage` (string, absolute), `$ogType` (string, default `website`), `$robotsOverride` (string), `$jsonLd` (array of ready JSON strings, default `[]`).
Inside `<head>`, after the description meta, print:
1. `<meta name="robots">`: `$robotsOverride` if not empty, else `$seo['robots_tag']` if set and not empty, else `index, follow`.
2. `<link rel="canonical">` only when `$canonicalUrl` is not empty.
3. Open Graph: `og:title` (`$seo['og_title']` → `$seo['seo_title']` → `$pageTitle`), `og:description` (`og_description` → `seo_description` → `$metaDescription`), `og:type`, `og:url` (= canonical, only if not empty), `og:site_name` = `GudangPC`, `og:image` only if `$seo['og_image']` or `$ogImage` is not empty (the first one that is absolute; if `og_image` is a relative path convert with `Seo::absoluteUrl`).
4. Twitter: `twitter:card` = `summary_large_image` when an image exists, else `summary`; `twitter:title` (`twitter_title` → og title), `twitter:description` (`twitter_description` → og description).
5. For each string in `$jsonLd`: `<script type="application/ld+json" nonce="<?= $nonce ?>">` + string + `</script>`. Then, if `$seo['schema_markup']` is not empty and `Seo::cleanJsonLd()` returns something, print that too (only when `$jsonLd` has no product schema; see B4, for now just print both).
6. `$seo['custom_head_tags']` raw, if not empty.
Right after the opening `<body>` tag print `$seo['custom_body']` raw if not empty. In `footer.php`, just before `</body>` print `$seo['custom_footer']` raw if not empty.

**Escaping note for the worker:** every value above goes through `htmlspecialchars((string) ...)` **except** the JSON-LD strings and the three admin-authored HTML fields (`custom_head_tags`, `custom_body`, `custom_footer`). Add a one-line comment above each of those four unescaped outputs saying why.

**Do not** change controllers in this task.

**Manual test:** with no controller changes, every page still renders and `view-source` shows `robots` and `og:site_name`; no PHP notices.

**`Seo` additions:**
- `breadcrumbJsonLd(array $crumbs): string`: `$crumbs` = list of `['label' => string, 'path' => string]` (last item may have an empty path). Returns BreadcrumbList JSON (absolute URLs via `absoluteUrl`; return `''` if `APP_URL` is empty).
- `productJsonLd(array $product, string $brandName, array $offers, string $path, string $imagePath): string`: `Product` with `name`, `description` (`plainText` of short description else description, 300), `image` (absolute, only if present), `brand` (`Brand` name, only if not empty), `mpn` = `model_number` (only if not empty), `url`, and `offers` as one `AggregateOffer` (`priceCurrency` `IDR`, `lowPrice`, `highPrice`, `offerCount`, `availability` `https://schema.org/InStock`). Return `''` if `$offers` is empty. **Never** emit `aggregateRating` or `review` (we have no first-party reviews; marketplace ratings must not be marked up).

**Controllers:** product page passes `jsonLd` = non-empty results of `productJsonLd` and `breadcrumbJsonLd` (Home › Category › Product). Category page: breadcrumb (Home › Category). Brand page: breadcrumb (Home › Brands › Brand). Also pass `breadcrumbs` (array for the visible partial).
**Partial `_breadcrumb.php`:** Bootstrap `breadcrumb` nav (`<nav aria-label="breadcrumb">`), items from `$breadcrumbs` (`label`, `url`; last item `active`, no link), all escaped. Include it at the top of the three views with `include`.
**Header rule:** when the product controller provides a product JSON-LD, the header must not also print `seo.schema_markup` for that page unless the user filled it (user value replaces the generated product schema). Adjust the B1 logic accordingly: custom `schema_markup` wins over generated Product schema; breadcrumbs always print.

**Manual test:**
1. Product page shows a breadcrumb and `view-source` has two JSON-LD blocks; paste the page into Google's Rich Results Test or schema.org validator: Product with offers and BreadcrumbList parse without errors.
2. Product with no active offers: no Product JSON-LD, breadcrumb only.
3. Fill a custom schema in the dashboard → it replaces the generated Product block.

   LEFT JOIN vendors v ON v.id = o.vendor_id

   INNER JOIN stores s ON s.id = o.store_id
   LEFT JOIN vendors v ON v.id = o.vendor_id

```

# PHASE D: Import engine

Background: the importer works as a first version but: it is **not transactional**, `vendor_slug` must be filled by hand (the scraper deliberately leaves it blank and writes `vendor_name`, which the importer ignores), `image_url` and `notes` columns from the scraper are ignored, the "affiliate_url" is just the raw marketplace URL (no commission link), offers are matched only by `(product, vendor)`, and there is no price history.

## D1: Migration for listing identity and affiliate templates

**Files created:** `database/migrations/021_offer_listing_identity_and_affiliate_template.sql`. SQL only; no PHP.

Use the idempotent `information_schema` check style of `014_add_indexes.sql` (or `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` as in 009/017/018):
```sql
ALTER TABLE offers
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_url text DEFAULT NULL AFTER affiliate_url,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS external_id varchar(100) DEFAULT NULL;
-- unique per marketplace listing; NULL external_id (legacy rows) is allowed many times
-- add UNIQUE KEY offers_store_external (store_id, external_id) only if it does not exist
ALTER TABLE stores
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS affiliate_url_template varchar(500) DEFAULT NULL;
```

**PO step:** run it. **Manual test:** `DESCRIBE offers; DESCRIBE stores;` show the new columns; existing pages still work.

## D2: Affiliate template field on marketplaces

**Files changed:** `AdminStoreController.php`, `views/dashboard/stores/create.php`, `views/dashboard/stores/edit.php`.

- New optional field `affiliate_url_template` (max 500). Validation: empty, or starts with `https://` and contains at least one placeholder from `{url}` (raw product URL) or `{url_encoded}` (URL-encoded raw product URL) or `{external_id}`. Anything else: error "Template must start with https:// and contain {url}, {url_encoded} or {external_id}."
- Add the helper text under the input: "Example: `https://affiliate-network.example/deeplink?to={url_encoded}&sub=gudangpc`. Leave empty to use the raw product URL."
- Wire it into create/update, the `old` repopulation and the edit form following the pattern already used for other store fields.

**Manual test:** save a store with a valid template, reload the edit page → value shown; invalid template → error and the form keeps what you typed.

## D3: Importer hardening

**Files changed:** `app/Core/ProductImporter.php` (protected, authorized), `app/Controllers/AdminProductImportController.php`, `views/dashboard/products/import.php`, and `bin/import_products.php` only if it reads report keys that change (read it first).

Implement all of the following inside `ProductImporter` (read the whole file before editing):

1. **Transaction:** `importFile` / `importRows` for a real run (not dry-run): `beginTransaction()` before the row loop, `commit()` after, and on any exception `rollBack()` then rethrow. Row-level rejections do **not** abort; they stay in the report.
2. **New CSV columns** (all optional): `source_url`, `external_id`. Header check still requires only `product_slug`.
3. **Required offer fields** become: `marketplace`; (`vendor_slug` **or** `vendor_name`); `price_idr`; (`affiliate_url` **or** `source_url`). Adjust the "offer fields filled" logic so a row that has only product columns is still a product-only row, and a partially filled offer row is still rejected as `incomplete offer data`.
4. **Seller auto-create:** if `vendor_slug` is empty and `vendor_name` is not: slug = lowercase `a-z0-9-` of `<marketplace>-<vendor_name>`; find by slug, else insert into `vendors` (`store_id`, `name`, `slug`, `status` = `active`, and `store_rating` when given). Count `created_vendors` in the report. If `vendor_slug` is given but unknown, keep today's rejection `unknown vendor`.
5. **Affiliate URL resolution:** if `affiliate_url` is empty, take the marketplace's `affiliate_url_template` (add a lookup by store id), replace `{url}`, `{url_encoded}` (`rawurlencode`), `{external_id}` using `source_url` / `external_id`. If the store has no template, use `source_url` and add a **warning** `no affiliate template for <marketplace>` (once per marketplace per run). Always store `source_url` on the offer when given.
6. **Matching offers:** if `external_id` is given, look the offer up by `(store_id, external_id)` first; if found and its `product_id` differs from the row's product, reject with `listing already linked to another product`. Otherwise fall back to the existing `(product_id, vendor_id)` lookup. If an offer is found by `(product_id, vendor_id)` and **both** the stored and the CSV `external_id` are non-empty and different, reject with `seller already has another listing for this product`. On update, store `external_id` and `source_url` when the offer had none.
7. **Scraper notes:** if the `notes` column exists and its value is not empty and not `ok` (case-insensitive), reject the row with `scraper note: <value>`.
8. **Price sanity warning:** on an update where the new price differs from the stored price by more than 50 % in either direction, still update, but add a warning `large price change: <slug> <old> -> <new>`.
9. **Report:** add `created_vendors` (int) and `warnings` (list of strings) to the returned array; keep every existing key.

`AdminProductImportController` and `import.php`: show `created_vendors`, and a Warnings card (only when not empty) listing the warnings. Keep the existing rejection table.

**Manual test** (use a copy of a real scraper CSV and `bin/scraper/test_import.csv`):
1. Row with `marketplace`, `vendor_name` only (no `vendor_slug`) imports and creates the seller.
2. Row with `notes` = `blocked_captcha` is rejected with that reason.
3. Break the file on purpose halfway (cause an exception, e.g. a column count the code cannot handle, or ask the worker for a safe way to simulate it) → nothing from that run is in the database.
4. A marketplace without a template shows the warning; after saving a template in D2, the stored `affiliate_url` follows the template.
5. Change a price by 60 % in the CSV → updated, warning listed.
6. Same `external_id` pointing at a different `product_slug` → rejected.

TASK: D3 - Importer hardening
FILES CHANGED:
- `app/Core/ProductImporter.php` - real runs wrap the whole row loop in one transaction (`beginTransaction()` / `commit()`, `rollBack()` + rethrow on any `Throwable`; row rejections do not abort). New optional CSV columns `source_url`, `external_id` (external id truncated to 100). Offer detection now counts marketplace, (vendor_slug or vendor_name), price_idr, (affiliate_url or source_url); product-only rows still take the product path and partial offer rows are rejected as `incomplete offer data`. Seller auto-create: when `vendor_slug` is empty, a slug is generated from `<marketplace>-<vendor_name>`, looked up, and inserted as `active` (with `store_rating` when supplied); `created_vendors` counted; known good vendors cached per run. Affiliate resolution: explicit `affiliate_url` wins; otherwise the store template replaces `{url_encoded}` (rawurlencode), `{url}`, `{external_id}`; without a template `source_url` is used and one `no affiliate template for <marketplace>` warning is added. `source_url`/`external_id` are always stored on created offers. Matching by `(store_id, external_id)` first (an early pre-check rejects `listing already linked to another product` before any vendor/product write), then `(product_id, vendor_id)`; a stored external id that differs from the CSV one rejects with `seller already has another listing for this product`; updates fill missing `external_id`/`source_url`. Rows with a `notes` value other than empty/`ok` are rejected with `scraper note: <value>`. Price changes above 50 % add `large price change: <slug> <old> -> <new>` while still updating. Report also returns `created_vendors` and `warnings`.
- `app/Controllers/AdminProductImportController.php` - success flash message includes the sellers created count.
- `views/dashboard/products/import.php` - reads `created_vendors` and `warnings`; added a "Sellers created" counter and a Warnings card (only when non-empty) above the rejection table.
